contract: EF Core 10 relational public API conformance
inventoryRule: A public API entry without an explicit disposition or linked behavioral test remains uncovered; inventory presence alone does not imply conformance.
capabilityRule: Capability declarations control applicability only and never modify expected results.

dispositionRules.reason: These are public query provider service and expression APIs. The suite does not invoke provider services directly; it verifies translation and results through public IQueryable operations.

These are public storage and type-mapping service APIs used by provider implementations. Their observable mapping behavior is exercised through persistence and type-fidelity tests rather than direct service calls.
These are public update pipeline service APIs used by provider implementations. Persistence behavior is tested through DbContext SaveChanges and other public application operations.
These are EF Core design-time and code-generation APIs; they do not define relational provider runtime behavior.
Diagnostic identifiers, event payloads, and logging helpers are owned by EF Core. Provider-observable interception behavior is covered through public SaveChanges tests where applicable.

These are EF Core fluent model-configuration APIs. Provider obligations concern the observable effect of the configured model, which is tested through schema, query, migration, and persistence behavior rather than each builder overload in isolation.
Model convention execution and convention set construction are owned by EF Core. Provider behavior is checked through the finalized model's observable schema and query behavior.
These are convention-time model metadata interfaces and extension points. This black-box suite does not invoke provider convention services directly.
Mutable model metadata APIs define EF Core model construction behavior. Providers are assessed by honoring the resulting model through public database operations.
Read-only model metadata APIs are owned by EF Core and are independent of relational provider execution behavior.
Runtime metadata implementation types are EF Core model infrastructure, not provider-specific public behavior.
These EF Core relational fluent APIs configure model metadata. Provider conformance is evaluated through observable behavior of models configured with those APIs.
These APIs inspect relational model metadata owned by EF Core. This suite does not test provider implementation details by inspecting metadata extensions.
These APIs inspect relational property metadata owned by EF Core. Provider mapping behavior is assessed through persistence and value-fidelity results.
These EF Core relational fluent APIs configure property metadata. Provider effects are evaluated through public queries, schema creation, migrations, and persistence.
These EF Core relational fluent APIs configure model metadata. Provider effects are evaluated through public database behavior.
These APIs inspect EF Core relational model metadata. The black-box contract checks resulting database behavior rather than metadata internals.
These APIs inspect EF Core relational type metadata. Provider behavior is checked through schema, query, and persistence results.
These EF Core model-building overloads configure primitive collection metadata; collection persistence and query results are the provider contract tested here.
These EF Core model-building overloads configure complex property metadata; provider obligations are assessed through complex value persistence and query behavior.
These EF Core model-building overloads configure complex primitive collection metadata; provider obligations are assessed through observable persistence and query behavior.
Relational annotation name constants are EF Core metadata identifiers and do not define provider runtime behavior.
This is an EF Core options service-extension implementation surface. The suite configures providers through public DbContextOptionsBuilder APIs and verifies resulting behavior.
This is an EF Core relational service-extension implementation surface. The suite configures providers through public options APIs and verifies resulting behavior.
This type maps EF Core internal service registrations and is outside the black-box provider boundary.
